Set PhysicsScene gravity and time step. For an explicitly selected scene, while stopped. No implicit scene creation or GPU/backend switch. On Newton it also sizes the solver's contact and constraint buffers, reported as newton_buffers, and without dt steps at 500 Hz. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): PhysicsScene prim path.
- `gravity` (array, default `[0, 0, -9.81]`): Acceleration vector in stage units/s^2.
- `dt` (number, optional): Physics timestep seconds, 1/1000..1/10. Default 1/60 on PhysX and 1/500 on Newton, the rate this project's Newton scenes use.
- `nconmax` (integer, optional): Newton only: MuJoCo-Warp contact buffer per world. Default: sized from the rigid-body count. Refused on PhysX.
- `njmax` (integer, optional): Newton only: constraint rows per world; same rules as nconmax.

### `sim__physics__contacts`

Listed as `sim__physics(action="contacts")`.

Read current contact pairs: PhysX impulses, or on Newton the last step's summed world-frame force in N on collider_a (impulse is null). For up to 32 bodies from the last delivered contact report. Subscribes on first use or Play. Only colliders with PhysxContactReportAPI report; others are listed with the fix, and none reporting refuses CONTACT_REPORT_DISABLED. Needs a playing or paused initialized timeline. Newton refuses CONTACT_QUERY_UNSUPPORTED only if forces are unavailable. No app update is pumped. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `paths` (array, required): 1..32 absolute rigid-body or collider paths.

### `sim__physics__inspect`

Listed as `sim__physics(action="inspect")`.

Report authored collision, body, mass and joints. A bounded report that includes articulations. Does not assert initialized or stable physics. On Newton it adds a newton section (configured buffers, active contacts and constraints against capacity, overflow flags) and warnings CONTACT_BUFFER_FULL, CONSTRAINT_BUFFER_FULL, NEWTON_SOLVER_OVERFLOW, NEWTON_SOLVER_NOT_CONVERGED. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `root` (string, default `"/"`): Absolute subtree path.
- `limit` (integer, default `100`): Maximum visited nodes 1..200.

### `sim__physics__raycast`

Listed as `sim__physics(action="raycast")`.

Cast one ray into the PhysX scene. Hits with position, normal, distance, collider and rigid-body paths. all=false returns the closest; all=true returns up to 32 sorted by distance. max_distance 0..100 stage units; direction is normalised and the result says so; scene_ready=false before physics initialises. Newton refuses RAYCAST_UNSUPPORTED. No app update is pumped. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `origin` (array, required): Ray origin [x, y, z] in world stage units.
- `direction` (array, required): Ray direction [x, y, z]; normalised before use.
- `max_distance` (number, default `100`): Maximum distance in stage units, >0 and <=100.
- `all` (boolean, default `false`): Return every hit up to 32 instead of only the closest.

### `sim__prim__bounds`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="bounds")`.

World-space bounds of one prim. At default USD time from UsdGeom.BBoxCache.ComputeWorldBound: axis-aligned min/max, centre and size, plus the oriented box's world corners; purpose selects default, render, proxy or guide geometry. Stage units; empty says the prim has no boundable content. Authored USD, not a runtime physics observation. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Absolute prim path.
- `purpose` (default|render|proxy|guide, default `"default"`): Geometry purpose whose bounds to measure.

### `sim__prim__clone`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="clone")`.

Clone a pack-created leaf primitive. A simple leaf primitive into a new path, preserving session-layer attributes. Refuses references, children, sensors and articulations. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Pack-created source leaf.
- `new_path` (string, required): New path, not in use yet.

### `sim__prim__create`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="create")`.

Create a primitive in the session layer. A Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Capsule, Cone, Plane, Xform or PhysicsScene. No arbitrary references/attributes. Stopped timeline, existing parent and no conflict required. Dimensions are stage units; optional mass or density authors PhysicsMassAPI on geometry. Undo a created prim with sim__prim__delete; sim__prim__revert undoes the attributes. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): New absolute prim path; every ancestor must already exist (create them with kind=Xform).
- `kind` (string, required): Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Capsule, Cone, Plane, Xform or PhysicsScene.
- `size` (number, default `1`): Positive cube edge, sphere/cylinder/capsule/cone diameter or height, or Plane width and length.
- `rigid` (boolean, default `false`): Author rigid body AND collider on geometry.
- `collision` (boolean, optional): Author a static collider without a rigid body (walls, floors, shelves).
- `scale` (array, optional): Three positive scale factors [x, y, z]: a 1 m Cube with scale [0.2, 6, 1] is a wall. Very flat floors can stop wheels; the result warns.
- `mass` (number, optional): Mass in kilograms (needs rigid=true).
- `density` (number, optional): Density in kg per cubic metre, instead of mass (needs rigid=true).
- `material` (string, optional): Path of a material from sim__material__create, bound as the prim is made; nothing is created if it cannot be bound.
- `position` (array, default `[0, 0, 0]`): Three finite coordinates in stage units.
- `orientation` (array, default `[1, 0, 0, 0]`): Unit quaternion [w,x,y,z].
- `frame` (string, default `"local"`): Pose frame: local or world.

### `sim__prim__create_many`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="create_many")`.

Create up to 200 prims in one call, all or none. A tower, wall, grid or room without one sim__prim__create per piece. Each item takes that tool's arguments plus an optional material path; defaults fills any key an item leaves out, except keys that do not apply to its kind (an Xform skips rigid, mass and material; listed in defaults_skipped). Ancestors must exist, timeline stopped. A failing item removes the earlier ones; the error keeps its code and names index and path. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `items` (array, required): 1 to 200 objects taking create's arguments; path is required, kind may come from defaults.
- `defaults` (object, optional): Optional arguments shared by every item, for example {kind: Cube, rigid: true, mass: 0.015, material: /World/Looks/Wood}. An item's own value wins; keys that do not apply to an item's kind (rigid, mass or material on an Xform) are skipped for it.

### `sim__prim__delete`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="delete")`.

Delete one pack-owned subtree from the session layer only. Requires stopped physics and confirm=true; exact owned sensors release their resources; sensor-containing subtrees and articulation roots are refused. Prims from an opened file are not pack-owned, even ones you made earlier: allow_foreign=true deactivates such a prim in the session layer instead (USD cannot remove another layer's opinions from there). It stays composed as inactive and keeps its path; a sim__stage__save copy omits it; source files never change. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Pack-owned root path, or any prim with allow_foreign=true.
- `confirm` (boolean, required): Explicit confirmation; false refuses.
- `allow_foreign` (boolean, default `false`): Also act on a prim these tools did not create in this session: deactivate it in the session layer (or remove it if all its opinions are session-layer ones). World/default prim, articulation and other protections still apply. Source files are unchanged.

### `sim__prim__find`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="find")`.

Bounded search of prim paths: `contains` is a literal substring (not a regex), `type_name` an exact type, `root` limits it to one subtree. Includes inactive prims. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `contains` (string, default `""`): Literal path substring <=128 characters.
- `type_name` (string, default `""`): Exact USD type or empty.
- `limit` (integer, default `100`): Maximum matches 1..200.
- `root` (string, default `"/"`): Only search under this prim, such as a robot's path. Default: the whole stage.

### `sim__prim__get`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="get")`.

Read a prim's transforms and authored physics. Local/world matrices and authored physics at default USD time. Runtime physics readiness remains unknown. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Absolute prim path.

### `sim__prim__measure`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="measure")`.

Distance between two prims' world bounds. At default USD time: centre-to-centre and the shortest gap (0 when the axis-aligned bounds overlap), in stage units, with each prim's axis-aligned bound. Refuses when either prim has no bounds, naming it and pointing to sim__prim__bounds. Authored USD, not runtime physics. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path_a` (string, required): First absolute prim path.
- `path_b` (string, required): Second absolute prim path.

### `sim__prim__revert`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="revert")`.

Undo this session's edits on a prim or subtree. Removes the session-layer opinions these tools authored on one prim or its subtree, restoring composed values from the source files, and reports what was removed and the values before and after. Source files never change. Prims the pack created stay: delete them with sim__prim__delete. Nothing recorded is a no-op, not an error. Only edits recorded in this session and stage can be undone. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Absolute prim path whose recorded edits are undone.
- `subtree` (boolean, default `true`): Also revert recorded edits on descendants.

### `sim__prim__set_attribute`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="set_attribute")`.

Set one typed attribute on any prim. In the session layer, reporting the composed value before and after; undo it with sim__prim__revert. Refuses engine- and schema-owned attributes (points, normals, faceVertexIndices, faceVertexCounts, extent, xformOpOrder, xformOp:*, physics:*, physx*:*), instance proxies and Kit runtime prims. type creates a missing attribute; without it the attribute must exist. Values are JSON; quaternions are [w,x,y,z]. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Absolute prim path.
- `attribute` (string, required): Attribute name, e.g. visibility, purposes, user:owner or a namespaced name.
- `value` (any, required): New value as JSON: true/false, a number, a string, or a flat list for a vector/quaternion. Converted to the attribute's USD type.
- `type` (string, optional): USD type for a new attribute: bool, int, uint, int64, uint64, float, double, string, token, float2/3/4, double2/3/4, int2/3, color3f/4f, normal3f, point3f, vector3f, quatf, quatd.

### `sim__prim__set_transform`

Listed as `sim__prim(action="set_transform")`.

Set a static pose on any Xformable prim. Local or world, in the session layer; reports the pose before and after; undo with sim__prim__revert. Refuses instance proxies (name the instance root), articulation links other than the root (moving a link breaks its joints), animated transforms, Kit runtime prims and a running or paused timeline. Authors one transform override, so source files never change. No claim of runtime teleportation. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): Absolute Xformable prim path.
- `scale` (array, optional): Positive XYZ scale in the requested pose frame. Omitted: keep the prim's current local scale, so moving a scaled table does not resize it.
- `position` (array, default `[0, 0, 0]`): Three finite coordinates in stage units.
- `orientation` (array, default `[1, 0, 0, 0]`): Unit quaternion [w,x,y,z].
- `frame` (string, default `"local"`): Pose frame: local or world.

### `sim__quick_start`

One call that builds a working scene, needing no IDs: a ground plane, physics scene, lights and a camera aimed at it, in the current stage if it is new and empty, otherwise a new one. With robot, called again on a scene it built, it adds the robot and keeps your objects. No real-robot wiring. Edits go to the session layer; sim__stage__save keeps them. The timeline stays stopped unless play=true. Refuses to drop unsaved edits unless discard_changes=true. Returns IDs, paths and next steps; on Newton a newton field (rate, buffers). For the UR5e work cell, use workcell__cell..

- `robot` (string, optional): Optional robot: a public name, <pack id>/<version>/<file.usd> or <pack id>/<version>/<file.urdf> (a verified file of a pack in the asset root), or an absolute path under an approved root, e.g. /approved/robot/model.xml: any file or folder assets__import_path reads. Public names come from the simulator's own assets root: ur5e, franka, unitree_h1, unitree_g1, turtlebot3_burger, carter_v1, nova_carter, jetbot, create3.
- `fixed_base` (boolean, optional): Robot files: fix the base to the world. Default: true for URDF and xacro; the file's own for MJCF and SDF. Pass false for a robot that drives or walks. A USD robot keeps what its file says.
- `xacro_args` (object, optional): With a xacro robot: values for its $(arg name), e.g. {"ur_type": "ur10e"}.
- `sdf_model` (string, optional): With an SDF that holds several models (a Gazebo world): the model to import.
- `environment` (string, optional): Optional. "warehouse": a 24 by 16 m warehouse (racks, aisles, docks) with the robot at the start of an aisle; default robot carter_v1. "jenga": a table, a 54-block giant Jenga tower and a Franka in a ready pose; the result names the blocks and a poke target. Plain USD boxes with colliders: nothing downloaded.
- `ros` (boolean, default `false`): With a robot: also run what sim__ros2_tf runs, and report the shell line that matches this simulator.
- `up_axis` (Z|Y, default `"Z"`): The stage's up axis. The ground, gravity and camera follow it. A robot file must match, or the call refuses with the values to pass. A URDF is always Z up in metres.
- `meters_per_unit` (number, default `1.0`): The stage's units, as a positive number (0.01 for centimetres). Ground size, gravity, camera distance and framing scale with it. A robot file must match.
- `play` (boolean, default `false`): Start the timeline after building.
- `discard_changes` (boolean, default `false`): Replace a stage with unsaved edits (they are lost).

### `sim__ros2_tf`

Build one ROS 2 graph for a robot, the same way every time: /clock (sim time), /joint_states, the static world->base_link (or world->odom + odometry for a mobile base) and the robot's link TF from Isaac. Rebuilds its own graph on each call, so no frame is ever published twice by this tool; reuses an existing /clock and reports other ROS 2 publishers in the scene. Timeline must be stopped; publishes while playing. Then use scripts/ros2_rviz_config.py and scripts/ros2_tf_doctor.py (docs/ROS2-RVIZ.md). Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `robot` (string, required): Robot prim at or above its articulation root.
- `base_link` (string, default `""`): Robot root link prim; default: a link named base_link, base_footprint or base.
- `base_frame` (string, default `""`): TF name for the base link; default: the base_link prim name.
- `base` (string, default `"fixed"`): fixed (arm on a table: static world->base) or mobile (odometry: world->odom->base).
- `world_frame` (string, default `"world"`): Root frame for RViz's Fixed Frame, e.g. world or map. Empty: publish no world link (a localization node provides map->odom).
- `link_frames` (string, default `"isaac"`): isaac: Isaac publishes every link frame. robot_state_publisher: Isaac publishes only /joint_states and the base link; run robot_state_publisher with the URDF. Never both.
- `extra_frames` (array, default `[]`): Up to 16 more prims (cameras, LiDARs, tool0) to publish; frame name = prim name. One mounted on a robot link, or any with a fixed base, is published once as a static transform from its pose now.
- `attach_to` (string, default `""`): For a robot that is its own articulation mounted on another (RG2 on a UR5e wrist): the parent link's prim. Publishes parent->base_link dynamically on every tick instead of a static world link, so it follows the arm. Call this tool once per articulation, with a namespace for this one.
- `namespace` (string, default `""`): ROS node namespace prepended to the topics.
- `joint_states_topic` (string, default `"joint_states"`): Joint state topic.
- `clock` (auto|publish|skip, default `"auto"`): auto: reuse an existing /clock, else publish one shared clock for all robots (two clocks make RViz reset constantly); publish: always keep the tool's clock; skip: never create one.

### `sim__simulation__run`

Listed as `sim__simulation(action="run")`.

Run your own controller in the physics loop as a job. Each step gets the body's state {step, time_s, dt, position, orientation_wxyz, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, mass, params} and returns {force, torque} for that step; with articulation also joints, and joint_efforts or joint_targets back. Steps exactly from a pause (mode=step), or follows a playing timeline (mode=play). Returns job_id: job_status(job_id, wait_s=30), job_cancel. Writes a CSV log; with camera a video. module:function is OPT-IN CODE EXECUTION in Kit; tcp:// runs none. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `body` (string, required): Rigid body the controller acts on, e.g. a drone's base link.
- `controller` (string, required): tcp://127.0.0.1:<port>: your own process, one JSON line per step each way (twinsmith.controller_server.serve is a ready-made server; start it with run_script). Or /abs/file.py:function or package.module:function, loaded into Kit: def f(state) returning {'force': [x, y, z]}; state has position, linear_velocity, mass, dt, time_s and params. Kit must have been launched with TWINSMITH_ENABLE_SCENE_SCRIPTS=1; if not, the call says so and nothing runs.
- `duration_s` (number, required): Simulated seconds to run, up to 3600. The controller can end sooner with done=true.
- `params` (object, optional): Passed to the controller as state['params'] each step, e.g. gains or a target.
- `frame` (world|body, default `"world"`): Frame of the returned force and torque, applied at the centre of mass: world (default) or body.
- `log` (array, optional): Fields to log: position, orientation, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, force, torque. Default: all. Numbers the controller returns under log become columns too.
- `log_every` (integer, default `1`): Log one row every this many physics steps, 1..10000.
- `filename` (string, optional): New CSV name in the output folder, e.g. hover.csv. Default run-<time>.csv. Never overwrites.
- `mode` (step|play, default `"step"`): step (default): exact steps from a paused timeline, repeatable and as fast as the machine allows. play: the timeline plays and the controller runs in the engine's pre-step callback, so ROS publishers and action graphs tick too; it keeps playing afterwards.
- `steps_per_frame` (integer, optional): Physics steps between app frames, 1..120. Default: about real time at 60 frames per second. With camera, fps sets it.
- `articulation` (string, optional): Articulation root of a jointed robot (often <robot>/root_joint). The state then has joints {names, positions, velocities}, and the controller may return joint_efforts, joint_targets or joint_velocity_targets as {joint name: value} (N m or N, rad or stage units).
- `observe` (array, optional): Up to 8 more rigid bodies whose state the controller gets under observed[path]. It may push them too, with wrenches: {path: {force, torque}}.
- `camera` (string, optional): Record this camera while it runs (from sim__camera__create): one frame per app frame, and job_status then gives video_path. Works headless and on a locked screen.
- `adopt` (boolean, optional): Record a camera that came with an opened scene (see sim__camera__capture adopt).
- `fps` (number, default `30`): With camera: video frames per simulated second, 1..60.
- `label` (string, optional): Short name for the job, shown by job_status and drawn on the video (<=80 characters).

### `sim__simulation__step`

Listed as `sim__simulation(action="step")`.

Advance exact physics steps while paused. 1..120 steps on PhysX or qualified Newton, PAUSED and initialized: from a stopped timeline, call sim__timeline action=initialize (physics may advance). No app-update pumping or engine fallback. Returns measured time delta, poses for observe_prims, DOFs for observe_joints. A failure after stepping reports the clock and phase. No retry or rollback. On Newton it first refuses STEP_DT_SOURCES_DISAGREE if the scene's timestep differs from Newton's, and adds a newton section. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `steps` (integer, required): Number of physics steps 1..120.
- `observe_prims` (array, default `[]`): Up to 16 rigid body paths.
- `observe_joints` (array, default `[]`): Up to 8 articulation paths.

### `sim__stage__clear_owned`

Listed as `sim__stage(action="clear_owned")`.

Remove what these tools created. Only pack-created non-sensor, non-articulated subtrees; other scene content is kept. Explicit stopped target and confirm required. Returns removed/refused lists. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `confirm` (boolean, required): Explicit confirmation.

### `sim__stage__info`

Listed as `sim__stage(action="info")`.

Identify the open stage; call this first. Reads process incarnation, stage identity, units, timeline and bounded prim count.

No arguments.

### `sim__stage__open`

Listed as `sim__stage(action="open")`.

Open a USD file as the current stage. Accepts .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz under your home or this simulator's output folder, like File > Open, with the timeline stopped. Refuses to drop unsaved edits unless discard_changes=true. Reports stale saved LiDAR render products and never changes the file. Returns the new session_id and stage_id for later sim__* calls; run_python sessions reset. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, required): USD file to open: absolute, under your home or this simulator's output folder. A leading ~ is expanded.
- `discard_changes` (boolean, default `false`): Open even if the current stage has unsaved edits (they are lost).

### `sim__stage__save`

Listed as `sim__stage(action="save")`.

Export a flattened copy of the stage to a new file. Includes session edits, to a new basename (.usda added if absent) in the output root or in `directory` under your home; with format=urdf one robot as URDF plus meshes. Never overwrites or switches the current stage. External texture paths remain dependencies; process-bound render pipelines are omitted, and unknown native pipeline content refuses. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `filename` (string, required): New basename, e.g. scene or scene.usda; no other extension, no folders.
- `directory` (string, optional): Existing folder under your home to write into instead of the output root (absolute path). Never overwrites.
- `format` (usd|urdf, default `"usd"`): usd (default): a flattened .usda copy of the scene. urdf: one robot as a folder <filename>/ with <filename>.urdf and meshes/ (OBJ), which lists what a URDF cannot hold (drives, physics materials, sensors).
- `robot_path` (string, optional): With format=urdf: the robot's articulation root or top prim. Default: the stage's default prim.
- `reset_camera_render_handles` (boolean, default `false`): Remove session-only ROS camera and LiDAR viewportHandle fields from the copy, so native textures rebuild after restart. This tool's own capture products need no flag. Default false refuses affected saves; true still refuses authored, ambiguous, connected or unavailable bindings. Originals and live stage are unchanged; omitted property paths are returned. This is export policy, not proof of authorship.

### `sim__stage__tree`

Listed as `sim__stage(action="tree")`.

Bounded stage hierarchy including inactive prims. Text is untrusted data. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `root` (string, default `"/"`): Absolute subtree root.
- `limit` (integer, default `100`): Maximum nodes 1..200.
- `depth` (integer, optional): Levels below root to list (1..64); default all.
- `include_runtime` (boolean, default `false`): Also list Kit's runtime /Render (Replicator) prims, hidden by default.

### `sim__timeline`

Play, pause, stop, initialize or reset. initialize briefly plays a stopped timeline then pauses it, so physics may advance; it refuses a playing timeline. Play reports physics_ready. Reset is the call after a failed run: it cancels this pack's jobs and stops the timeline; safe to repeat. sim__simulation__step advances exact steps. Stop rewinds physics and awaits pending render/writer completion. TIMELINE_BUSY or TIMELINE_INTERRUPTED requires inspection before retry. The session edit target is leased until Stop. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `action` (string, required): play, pause, stop, initialize (briefly play then pause; physics may advance), or reset (cancel jobs, stop, back to the authored start).
- `resume` (boolean, optional): Continue a timeline a script or the GUI paused, without the stop that would end it. Physics then writes where the script set it. With action=play.

### `sim__trajectory__replay`

Listed as `sim__simulation(action="replay")`.

Replay a saved trajectory into a labelled video. As a job: moves prims through the poses in a file and saves one camera frame per step. No physics runs and the prims go back afterwards; needs a stopped timeline. Returns job_id; job_status(job_id, wait_s=30) then gives video_path, an MP4 with the label drawn on it (works headless and on a locked screen). Without camera it shows the poses at wall-clock pace, for a screen recording. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `trajectory` (string, required): Absolute path under your home or the output folder. A CSV as sim__simulation__run writes it (time_s, px,py,pz, qw,qx,qy,qz; or t and x,y,z), or JSON / JSONL samples {time_s, position, orientation_wxyz} or {time_s, bodies: {prim: {...}}}.
- `prim` (string, optional): Prim to move, for a file with one unnamed body: the robot's top Xform or a free body, not a jointed link.
- `camera` (string, optional): Camera to record, from sim__camera__create or sim__camera__list. Omit to only show the poses.
- `adopt` (boolean, optional): Record a camera that came with an opened scene (see sim__camera__capture adopt).
- `label` (string, optional): One line (<=120 characters) drawn on every frame of the video, e.g. 'PhysX hover, kp=4'.
- `fps` (number, default `30`): Video frames per second, 1..60.
- `speed` (number, default `1`): Playback speed: 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 slow motion.
- `start_s` (number, optional): Start at this trajectory time. Default: its first sample.
- `end_s` (number, optional): End at this trajectory time. Default: its last sample.
- `filename` (string, optional): New video name, e.g. hover.mp4. Default replay-<time>.mp4. Frames are saved beside it as <name>-00001.png.

### `sim__ui__act`

Listed as `sim__ui(action="act")`.

Click or type in Isaac Sim's UI; can delete data. Drives Isaac Sim's own UI through Kit's input system, not the desktop: click, double_click, right_click, move, drag, scroll, type, keypress, menu, tab, close, or wait. Target a widget by ref from sim__ui__find or by x, y window pixels. Works while the desktop is locked or used remotely (the X11 computer tool does not). screenshot_after=true returns the window after the action; or check with sim__ui__find. UI actions can change or delete scene data and files like a person clicking would.

- `action` (click|double_click|right_click|move|drag|scroll|type|keypress|menu|tab|close|wait, optional): What to do. tab brings a docked window to the front, like clicking its tab (sim__ui__find lists hidden_tabs); close hides a Kit window or docked panel such as 'Console' and reports whether it is now hidden (reopen with tab). Omit it with actions.
- `ref` (string, optional): Widget ref from sim__ui__find (its centre is used). For type/keypress it is clicked first to focus it.
- `x` (integer, optional): X in Isaac Sim window pixels (when no ref).
- `y` (integer, optional): Y in Isaac Sim window pixels (when no ref).
- `end_x` (integer, optional): Drag end X in window pixels.
- `end_y` (integer, optional): Drag end Y in window pixels.
- `text` (string, optional): Text for action=type (1..500 characters, no newlines; send enter with keypress).
- `keys` (array, optional): For action=keypress: one key plus optional modifiers, e.g. ["ctrl", "s"], ["enter"], ["shift", "tab"].
- `window` (string, optional): Window or tab title for tab and close, e.g. 'Console'.
- `menu` (string, optional): For action=menu: a menu path, e.g. 'Create/Mesh/Cube' (a menu an extension adds exists only once it has loaded), or a top-level menu such as 'Layouts' (opened to list its items, then closed again).
- `scroll_x` (integer, default `0`): Horizontal wheel steps for action=scroll (-20..20).
- `scroll_y` (integer, default `0`): Vertical wheel steps for action=scroll (-20..20; negative scrolls down).
- `frames` (integer, default `3`): Frames to wait after the action so the UI updates (0..600).
- `actions` (array, optional): Batch of up to 10 steps, each an object with action (not sub_action) and that action's arguments. E.g. [{"action": "click", "ref": "..."}, {"action": "type", "text": "2"}]. Steps run in order and stop at the first failure; they replace the top-level action fields, and frames is then each step's default wait.
- `coord_space` (string, default `"window"`): window (Isaac Sim window pixels) or the coord_space token a screenshot printed (x/y are then pixels of that image).
- `screenshot_after` (boolean, default `false`): Also return a screenshot of the Isaac Sim window after the action(s).
- `find_after` (string, optional): Also return up to 10 widgets matching this text after the action(s), compactly (same matching as sim__ui__find query).

### `sim__ui__find`

Listed as `sim__ui(action="find")`.

Find Isaac Sim UI widgets. Lists Isaac Sim's own UI widgets (buttons, fields, checkboxes, combo boxes, tree views, and labels when a query is given) with their text, tooltip, current value, a ref, and their centre in pixels of the Isaac Sim window (the same pixels as screenshot(window_id=<Isaac Sim window>)), plus the visible Kit windows. Works while the desktop is locked or used remotely. Use the ref with sim__ui__act instead of guessing coordinates.

- `query` (string, default `""`): Case-insensitive text to match in a widget's name, text, tooltip, identifier or type, e.g. 'play' or 'Add'. Empty lists interactive widgets only.
- `window` (string, default `""`): Only windows whose title contains this, e.g. 'Stage'.
- `limit` (integer, default `40`): Maximum widgets returned, 1..100 (the reply is also capped near 48 KB).
- `zoom_ref` (string, optional): Zoom on this widget ref instead of listing: returns an enlarged crop of the Isaac Sim window around it, with its own coord_space token.

### `sim__viewport`

Point the active viewport camera, e.g. before a screenshot. path alone frames a prim; path+margin frames its bounds plus margin metres; eye+target places the camera exactly; follow tracks the prim. Edits only the active camera in the session layer, with no undo entry. framed_path is the prim this call framed; the Stage selection is put back afterwards, so the Stage and Property panels keep their own selection. Refuses look-through targets and empty bounds, listing candidates. Does not wait for rendered pixels. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `path` (string, default `""`): Absolute prim path to frame or follow.
- `margin` (number, optional): Extra radius in metres around the prim's bounding sphere (0..1000), e.g. 1.0 for a small robot that will drive around.
- `eye` (array, optional): Camera position [x, y, z] in world coordinates (stage units).
- `target` (array, optional): Point to look at [x, y, z] in world coordinates (stage units); default: the prim's centre.
- `follow` (boolean, optional): true: follow path while playing (until stopped); false: stop following.
- `layout` (clean|default, optional): clean: hide the app's panels, menus, grid and selection outline for a recording. default: put them back. Alone, it leaves the camera where it is.
- `caption` (string, optional): One line (<=120 characters) drawn over the bottom of the viewport, e.g. the run's name, for screenshots and screen recordings; an empty string removes it. Needs a viewport window.

### `stat_file`

Listed as `files(action="stat")`.

Check a file's existence, size and sha256 on the bridge's box. Skips unchanged pushes and verifies assets.

- `path` (string, required): Path on the bridge's box (~ expands).

### `workcell__jenga_build`

Listed as `workcell__jenga(action="build")`.

Replace the Jenga tower in the current workcell on a stopped timeline using configured or overridden variation. Resamples blocks; not a physics-state reset.

- `profile` (string, optional): Optional name in jenga.variation_profiles; omitted uses the configured variation_profile.
- `seed` (integer, optional): Optional integer seed; omitted uses the configured variation_seed. A selected profile requires a seed.

### `workcell__jenga_status`

Listed as `workcell__jenga(action="status")`.

Read Jenga build details from the workcell report.

No arguments.

### `workcell__perception_status`

Listed as `workcell__perception(action="status")`.

Read camera build details; this does not capture sensor data.

No arguments.

### `workcell__robot_status`

Listed as `workcell__robot(action="status")`.

Read robot build details from the workcell report.

No arguments.

### `workcell__robot_wrench`

Listed as `workcell__robot(action="wrench")`.

Read the simulated Bota F/T sensor (its mount joint's reaction, sensor frame, N and N m) on PhysX or Newton, with the engine's mass of everything below the sensor and its weight. Needs an initialized, paused or playing simulation; not gravity-compensated or hardware-calibrated.

No arguments.

### `workcell__workcell_quick_start`

Listed as `workcell__cell(action="quick_start")`.

Build a stopped workcell from an external asset pack, on PhysX or Newton (Newton uses the config's per-engine drives; mirror_real needs PhysX). Refuses unsaved stage changes unless explicitly allowed. Returns a summary; action=status returns the full report.

- `config_path` (string, optional): Optional hardware configuration path.
- `mode` (physics|mirror_real, default `"physics"`): Physics mode, or zero-gravity mirror mode.
- `discard_changes` (boolean, default `false`): Allow replacement of an unsaved stage.
- `environment` (none|simple_room, default `"none"`): A room around the cell: simple_room references NVIDIA's Simple Room from the Isaac Sim assets server (needs network), floor level with the bench feet.

### `workcell__workcell_shutdown`

Listed as `workcell__cell(action="shutdown")`.

Release workcell state without clearing the stage.

No arguments.

### `workcell__workcell_status`

Listed as `workcell__cell(action="status")`.

Read the current workcell build report.

No arguments.

<a id="assets"></a>

## `assets`: Import and manage assets

Toolset `assets` is off until you select it with `+assets`. Reference: [ASSET-IMPORT.md](ASSET-IMPORT.md). 16 tools, listed as 5: `assets__import_path`, `assets__library` (roots, scan, search, info), `assets__mesh` (inspect, decimate, hulls, split), `assets__pack` (list, doctor, dependencies, adopt, pin, build), `assets__validate`.

### `assets__dependencies`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="dependencies")`.

Compute dependency closures for files under an approved root or the asset root. USD uses UsdUtils.ComputeAllDependencies through a host helper (TWINSMITH_USD_PYTHON) or else the selected Kit; native USD parsing is NOT sandboxed. A .urdf is read on the host with the build's package rules and returns its meshes, textures and package.xml, so a missing package is reported instead of a parser error. Copies nothing.

- `paths` (array, required): Absolute USD or URDF file paths, 1 to 64.

### `assets__import_path`

The one import for any robot or asset file: USD, URDF, xacro, SDF (Gazebo), MuJoCo MJCF (.xml), a mesh prop (glTF, GLB, OBJ, STL, FBX, PLY), a ROS map (.yaml, as walls), or a folder that holds one. format=auto picks it from the name; a folder names its own entry file, or the refusal lists the candidates. Xacro and SDF are converted on the host, never by running their code. Under an approved root or a pack; sources never change. Robot formats take fixed_base and default_drives. A USD reports its drawn `visuals`; none is a warning. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute path of the file, or of a folder that holds one, inside an approved root or a pack version of your asset root. Or use root_id with relative_path.
- `root_id` (string, optional): Approved root ID from assets__roots, with relative_path, instead of source_path.
- `relative_path` (string, optional): Path of the file or folder inside that root.
- `prim_path` (string, required): New absolute wrapper prim path; parent must exist.
- `format` (string, default `"auto"`): auto (default): from the file name, or from what the folder holds. Or usd, urdf, xacro, sdf, mjcf, mesh, map to say it.
- `xacro_args` (object, optional): For xacro: values for its $(arg name), e.g. {"ur_type": "ur10e"}. Names the file declares are in the result.
- `sdf_model` (string, optional): For an SDF with several models (a Gazebo world): the model to import. Left out, a refusal lists them.
- `fixed_base` (boolean, optional): Robot formats: fix the base to the world. Default: true for URDF and xacro; the model's own setting for SDF (a static model); the file's own for MJCF. Pass false for a robot that drives or walks.
- `joint_targets` (object, optional): Robot formats: start in a pose. {joint name: radians, or stage units for a sliding joint}, set as drive targets; unknown names are listed in the warnings.
- `scale` (number, optional): Mesh files: multiply the size (the file's unit to metres, e.g. 0.001 for millimetres). Default 1: metres.
- `up_axis` (string, optional): Mesh files: the file's own up axis, y or z. Default auto: glTF, GLB, FBX and OBJ are Y-up, STL and PLY Z-up; the result is Z-up.
- `as_collider` (string, optional): Mesh files: none (default, looks only), convex_hull or convex_decomposition collision shapes.
- `wall_height` (number, optional): ROS map (.yaml): wall height in metres. Default 1.
- `mass` (number, optional): Mesh files: kilograms; makes it a dynamic rigid body (with a convex hull collider unless you pick one).
- `default_drives` (boolean, optional): Author drives that hold a pose. URDF, xacro, SDF: default true (they have none). MJCF: default false; true gives joints with no drive (torque motors) a generic holding drive. Wheels and casters stay free.
- `position` (array, optional): Three finite coordinates in stage units. Omit it for a robot format: the robot is then raised out of any ground plane (up to 3 m); a given position is used as is, with a warning if it starts inside the ground. USD files go to the origin.
- `orientation` (array, default `[1, 0, 0, 0]`): Unit quaternion [w,x,y,z].
- `frame` (string, default `"local"`): Pose frame: local or world.

### `assets__info`

Listed as `assets__library(action="info")`.

Inspect a USER-TRUSTED project on the selected Kit. Takes a snapshot of it. Native USD parsing is NOT sandboxed. Refuses untrusted profiles and unresolved/outside snapshot dependencies. Requires session_id and stage_id from sim__stage__info.

- `session_id` (string, required): Exact session_id from sim__stage__info (call it first; process incarnation).
- `stage_id` (string, required): Exact stage_id from sim__stage__info (call it first); stale stages are refused.
- `root_id` (string, required): Approved trusted project root ID.
- `relative_path` (string, required): Relative path of the USD file within that root.

### `assets__mesh_decimate`

Listed as `assets__mesh(action="decimate")`.

Write a copy of a USD file whose render meshes are decimated (quadric) into a new folder, as a job. For render cost; it does not fix a collider overflow (use split). The source is never changed. Normals and texture coordinates of a decimated mesh are blocked because they no longer match its faces.

- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute USD file under an approved root or the asset root; or give pack and asset_id.
- `pack` (string, optional): "<pack id>/<version>" holding asset_id. Default: the project file's pack.
- `asset_id` (string, optional): Asset id of a file in pack, e.g. bench.
- `prims` (array, optional): Only meshes at or under these prim paths.
- `output` (string, required): New absolute folder under an approved root, outside the asset root.
- `target_tris` (integer, optional): About this many triangles in all, shared by mesh size. Give this or ratio.
- `ratio` (number, optional): Keep this fraction of each mesh's triangles, above 0 and at most 1. Give this or target_tris.

### `assets__mesh_hulls`

Listed as `assets__mesh(action="hulls")`.

Write a collision layer for a USD file into a new folder, as a job: for each mesh, <parent>/<mesh>_collision with an oriented box or convex hulls (purpose guide, CollisionAPI, convexHull approximation), in the mesh parent's frame so rigid bodies and joints are untouched. Shapes go to the meshes under prims; else to the file's mesh colliders; else, when no mesh is a collider, to every mesh. Sublayer it over the asset, or use split for the composed result.

- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute USD file under an approved root or the asset root; or give pack and asset_id.
- `pack` (string, optional): "<pack id>/<version>" holding asset_id. Default: the project file's pack.
- `asset_id` (string, optional): Asset id of a file in pack, e.g. bench.
- `prims` (array, optional): Only meshes at or under these prim paths.
- `output` (string, required): New absolute folder under an approved root, outside the asset root.
- `method` (string, default `"box"`): box (oriented box per mesh), convex (one hull), coacd (decomposition) or auto (box unless over twice the hull's volume, then coacd).
- `max_hulls` (integer, default `16`): coacd/auto: most convex pieces per mesh, 1 to 256.
- `threshold` (number, default `0.05`): coacd/auto: concavity, 0.01 to 1; lower is finer and slower.

### `assets__mesh_inspect`

Listed as `assets__mesh(action="inspect")`.

Report every mesh of a USD file: triangles, bounds, closed or not, whether it is a collider and its approximation, and totals including the triangles in triangle-mesh colliders (what overflows Newton). Read-only; parses USD in a subprocess of this server's interpreter (the mesh extra). Native USD parsing is not sandboxed.

- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute USD file under an approved root or the asset root; or give pack and asset_id.
- `pack` (string, optional): "<pack id>/<version>" holding asset_id. Default: the project file's pack.
- `asset_id` (string, optional): Asset id of a file in pack, e.g. bench.
- `prims` (array, optional): Only meshes at or under these prim paths.

### `assets__mesh_split`

Listed as `assets__mesh(action="split")`.

Write a USD asset as a render layer and a collision layer plus the file that composes them, into a new folder, as a job: <stem>_render (the source; the replaced meshes lose their collision schemas, other colliders stay), <stem>_collision.usdc (explicit shapes, purpose guide) and <stem>.usda (sublayers both, keeps the units, up axis and default prim). Point an asset at <stem>.usda; make it a pack version with assets__pack action=build. The source is never changed.

- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute USD file under an approved root or the asset root; or give pack and asset_id.
- `pack` (string, optional): "<pack id>/<version>" holding asset_id. Default: the project file's pack.
- `asset_id` (string, optional): Asset id of a file in pack, e.g. bench.
- `prims` (array, optional): Only meshes at or under these prim paths.
- `output` (string, required): New absolute folder under an approved root, outside the asset root.
- `collision` (object, optional): Collision shape options: method, max_hulls, threshold (as for hulls).

### `assets__pack_adopt`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="adopt")`.

Copy a folder into a new pack version. Copies a folder's asset files into a NEW pack version <id>/<version> in the asset root and write its pack.yaml (sha256 of every file, plus the source and license you give; redistributable is false unless you say so). The source must be under a user-approved root. A version that exists is never modified: give a new one. Symlinks are never followed. With from_old, converts an old-format pack folder of the asset root into <id>/v1, leaving the old files in place.

- `pack` (string, required): The new pack as "<pack id>/<version>", for example my-robot/v1.
- `source` (string, required): Where the files came from, one line (a vendor, repository URL and commit, or file hash). Recorded for every file.
- `license` (string, required): The licence or terms, one line (for example "private lab use only"). Recorded for every file.
- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute folder under an approved root. Give this or from_old.
- `from_old` (string, optional): Name of an old-format pack folder in the asset root to convert; pack must be <that name>/<version>.
- `redistributable` (boolean, default `false`): The files may be redistributed. Default false.
- `include` (array, optional): Extra file extensions to copy.
- `files` (array, optional): Copy only these files or folders, relative to source_path. A named file is copied whatever its type.
- `dry_run` (boolean, default `false`): Report the plan and write nothing.

### `assets__pack_build`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="build")`.

Copy asset files and their dependencies into a new pack version. USD, URDF, MuJoCo XML, SDF, mesh or ROS map files and only what they depend on go into a NEW pack version in the asset root, keeping layout, and write its pack.yaml. A file copied out of from_pack keeps that pack's source, license and redistributable; any other file needs source and license. Sources must be under an approved root or the asset root. Unresolved or remote references refuse the build unless allow_unresolved=true. An existing version is never modified. For xacro use assets__import_path.

- `pack` (string, required): Destination as "<pack id>/<version>"; the version must not exist.
- `sources` (array, required): USD, URDF, MJCF (.xml), SDF, mesh or map (.yaml) files, 1 to 64: absolute paths, or paths inside from_pack. A USD scene outside from_pack and layout_root is read for its references and not copied.
- `from_pack` (string, optional): Pack as "<pack id>/<version>" that source names and logical references come from. It must verify.
- `layout_root` (string, optional): Absolute folder the pack layout is relative to. Default: from_pack; for a USD the source's folder; for a URDF the approved root or pack holding it, which is also where its ROS packages are looked for.
- `source` (string, optional): Where files that do not come from from_pack came from, one line.
- `license` (string, optional): Licence or terms of those files, one line.
- `redistributable` (boolean, default `false`): Those files may be redistributed. Default false.
- `allow_unresolved` (boolean, default `false`): Build despite missing or remote references, and record them in pack.yaml.
- `dry_run` (boolean, default `false`): Report the closure and write nothing.

### `assets__pack_doctor`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="doctor")`.

Check a pack without changing it. Every file listed in pack.yaml exists and matches its sha256, nothing unlisted or symlinked is in the folder, then the dependencies of its USD, URDF, MJCF, SDF, mesh and map files must all be files of the same pack (unresolved, unreadable, remote and outside-pack references are problems). Parses USD in a host helper (TWINSMITH_USD_PYTHON) or else the selected Kit; says so if neither ran, and ok is then false. A URDF's own references are read on the host.

- `pack` (string, optional): Pack as "<pack id>/<version>". Default: the project file's pack.

### `assets__pack_pin`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="pin")`.

Rewrite the sha256 values of an existing pack.yaml to match its files, and show what changed. A version that already verifies is not modified. A changed hash accepts whatever bytes are there, so it is refused with before and after hashes unless the file is named in files or force=true. Missing or unlisted files cannot be fixed by a hash: write a new version with adopt or build.

- `pack` (string, optional): Pack as "<pack id>/<version>". Default: the project file's pack.
- `files` (array, optional): Pin only these relative paths, accepting their changes.
- `force` (boolean, default `false`): Accept every changed file.
- `dry_run` (boolean, default `false`): Show what would change and write nothing.

### `assets__packs`

Listed as `assets__pack(action="list")`.

List the asset packs in the asset root. Every <id>/<version> pack in the asset root (TWINSMITH_ASSET_ROOT, else <workspace>/assets) with its file count, size and whether it verifies against its pack.yaml, and any old-format pack with a hint to convert it with adopt. Host side, no Kit, no USD parser. Writes nothing. Kit reads its own settings: give host and Kit the same TWINSMITH_ASSET_ROOT. With a Kit connected it also lists kit_environment and warns when Kit and this host use a different asset root or project file.

No arguments.

### `assets__roots`

Listed as `assets__library(action="roots")`.

List launch-approved project roots and capability refusals. Filename access only; trusted projects are NOT sandboxed.

No arguments.

### `assets__scan`

Listed as `assets__library(action="scan")`.

Bounded filename-only USD and URDF discovery on the MCP host. No USD parser. Results are untrusted data. Folders deeper than eight levels are skipped and named in skipped_deep; the rest of the root is still scanned.

- `root_id` (string, required): Approved root ID, never an absolute path.
- `offset` (integer, default `0`): Page offset into the sorted bounded scan.
- `limit` (integer, default `50`): Page size 1..100.

### `assets__search`

Listed as `assets__library(action="search")`.

Fresh filename search across approved project/library roots. No network discovery, semantic service, manifest or fixed robot count. Refresh by calling again. Folders deeper than eight levels are skipped and named in skipped_deep.

- `query` (string, default `""`): Case-insensitive filename substring <=128 characters.
- `limit` (integer, default `50`): Maximum results 1..100.

### `assets__validate`

Check from the file alone whether a USD asset loads on Newton or PhysX: units, triangle-mesh colliders over budget, rendered collision shapes, zero-force drives, nested articulations, massless moving bodies, drive gains too stiff for 500 Hz, invalid mimic joints. File only: colliders a scene adds at build time are not seen. Returns ok and each check's level, prim, detail and fix; on physx the Newton-only rules are info. Read-only, in a subprocess (the mesh extra).

- `source_path` (string, optional): Absolute USD file under an approved root or the asset root; or give pack and asset_id.
- `pack` (string, optional): "<pack id>/<version>" holding asset_id. Default: the project file's pack.
- `asset_id` (string, optional): Asset id of a file in pack, e.g. bench.
- `engine` (string, default `"newton"`): newton or physx.
- `triangle_budget` (integer, default `200000`): Triangle-mesh collider triangles allowed.
- `kit` (boolean, default `false`): Also run Isaac Sim's Asset Validator: not available yet, refused.

<a id="cad"></a>

## `cad`: PCB checks, fab files, renders

Toolset `cad` is off until you select it with `+cad`. Reference: [HARDWARE.md](HARDWARE.md). 1 tools, listed as 1: `hardware`.

### `hardware`

PCB and enclosure outputs from tools beside twinsmith; no simulator. status: versions, pins, gaps. check: KiCad ERC and DRC counts (the board's own schematic). fab: check, then KiKit JLCPCB/PCBWay files, board.step and board.glb in a new folder; never uploads or orders. render: a Blender job that uses the GPU (follow with jobs). Inputs in approved folders only.

- `action` (Literal['status', 'check', 'fab', 'render'], required): Action to perform.
- `board` (str | None, default `None`): check/fab: absolute .kicad_pcb path inside an approved folder.
- `vendor` (Literal['jlcpcb', 'pcbway'], default `'jlcpcb'`): fab: which fab house's file set KiKit writes. Nothing is sent to it.
- `inputs` (list[str] | None, default `None`): render: absolute .glb, .gltf or .stl paths (GLB in metres, STL in millimetres).
- `name` (str | None, default `None`): fab/render: new folder name under <workspace>/runs/hardware; default a timestamp.
- `width` (int, default `1600`): render: image width in pixels.
- `height` (int, default `1200`): render: image height in pixels.
- `samples` (int, default `128`): render: Cycles samples per pixel.
- `allow_concurrent_gpu` (bool, default `False`): render: knowingly start next to another GPU job or a running simulator.

<a id="real2sim"></a>

## `real2sim`: RoboSimStudio real-to-sim and MuJoCo sysid

Toolset `real2sim` is off until you select it with `+real2sim`. Reference: [ROBOSIM.md](ROBOSIM.md). 2 tools, listed as 2: `robosim`, `sysid`.

### `robosim`

RoboSimStudio real-to-sim in its own Python, no Isaac bridge needed. start a scene from plain-data template (frozen until update_scene), reference a clip, compare, tune_push, rollout, compare_take, report, stop. Compares images; no mass or friction fitting. Scene code is not sandboxed; cuda:0 uses the GPU. Long actions: poll status.

- `action` (Literal['status', 'start', 'scene_template', 'update_scene', 'reference', 'snapshot', 'compare', 'rollout', 'tune_push', 'compare_take', 'stop', 'report'], required): Action to perform.
- `run` (str | None, default `None`): Exact run name from start. status: omit for a compact list. scene_template: write the file there.
- `name` (str | None, default `None`): start: short run name; letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.
- `scene` (str | None, default `None`): start/update_scene, advanced: absolute trusted scene .py (runs code, not sandboxed). Else use template.
- `device` (Literal['cpu', 'cuda:0'] | None, default `None`): start (required): cpu is plain MuJoCo, cuda:0 is Newton MuJoCo-Warp. Runs inherit it.
- `video` (str | None, default `None`): reference: absolute local video file; copied before extracting frames.
- `keys` (list[str] | None, default `None`): compare/compare_take: RSS object masks, e.g. ['block=red'] or ['block=#d01a10~0.1'].
- `take` (str | None, default `None`): rollout/compare_take: take name. tune_push: base name; trials are NAME-1, NAME-2.
- `routine` (str | None, default `None`): rollout: 'push' (default in the template) or 'settle', or a routine your scene defines.
- `camera` (str | None, default `None`): Camera name from start's RSS status; omit for the scene's first camera.
- `at` (str | None, default `None`): reference: RSS anchors in clip seconds, e.g. '0:start,3:middle,6:end'; default from start_s/end_s.
- `shape` (Literal['box', 'tee', 'jenga'], default `'tee'`): scene_template: tee, box or jenga, unless template gives a shape.
- `push` (dict | None, default `None`): rollout/tune_push: {'waypoints': [[s, x, y], ...] pusher path in m, 'object_velocity': [vx, vy, wz]}.
- `duration_s` (float | None, default `None`): rollout: simulated seconds; default the last waypoint time. Not with steps.
- `steps` (int | None, default `None`): rollout: control steps instead of duration_s.
- `record_fps` (float, default `10.0`): rollout: frames per simulated second to record (nearest whole step stride).
- `start_s` (float | None, default `None`): reference: clip window start; compare_take: clip window start (default: reference's).
- `end_s` (float | None, default `None`): reference/compare_take: clip window end in seconds.
- `sim_start_s` (float | None, default `None`): compare_take: simulated time matching start_s; default 0.
- `sim_end_s` (float | None, default `None`): compare_take: simulated time matching end_s; default same length as the clip window.
- `size` (str, default `'320x240'`): snapshot/compare: WIDTHxHEIGHT pixels.
- `width` (int, default `320`): reference: contact-sheet tile width.
- `port` (int | None, default `None`): start: viewer port; omit to pick a free one. RSS listens on all interfaces.
- `wait_s` (float, default `0`): Wait at most this many seconds; poll status with run for completion.
- `allow_concurrent_gpu` (bool, default `False`): start: knowingly permit cuda:0 despite other GPU workloads or an unavailable GPU check.
- `template` (dict | None, default `None`): start/update_scene/scene_template: plain data {shape, size, position [x,y], yaw, color, camera, push}.
- `all` (bool, default `False`): status without run: every run in full, not live servers and the 5 newest.
- `max_trials` (int | None, default `None`): tune_push: most rollouts to try (default 6, at most 12).

### `sysid`

Fit model parameters (joint damping, armature, friction loss, position gains, geom mass and friction) to recorded trajectories with MuJoCo's system identification, in its own environment on the CPU. No simulator bridge needed. fit runs a job; follow it with jobs, then report. Reads only an approved dataset folder with a SOURCE.md; nothing here reads a robot.

- `action` (Literal['status', 'fit', 'report'], required): status: the environment, its MuJoCo against the pin, recent fits. fit: start a fit job. report: read a fit.
- `dataset` (str | None, default `None`): fit: absolute dataset folder inside a user-approved root: model.xml, params.json, episodes/*.npz, SOURCE.md.
- `name` (str | None, default `None`): fit/report: the fit's name; its folder is <workspace>/runs/sysid/<name>/.
- `holdout` (list[str] | None, default `None`): fit: episodes (file names without .npz) kept out of the fit and scored after it.
- `max_iters` (int, default `50`): fit: optimiser iterations at most.
- `timeout_s` (float, default `3600.0`): fit: the job is stopped after this many seconds.

<a id="planning"></a>

## `planning`: Graph-as-Policy skill graphs

Toolset `planning` is off until you select it with `+planning`. Reference: [PLANNING-EVAL.md](PLANNING-EVAL.md#gap). 1 tools, listed as 1: `gap`.

### `gap`

Graph-as-Policy skill graphs, from its own pinned checkout: status (checkout, GPU, keys), tools (the skill catalog), check (which tool bundles are ready), validate (a graph's structure and skill contracts; no GPU or model, for a graph you wrote), generate (a graph from an instruction; calls a paid model, only when the owner allows it), run (a graph in simulation, as a job; uses the GPU). Never --real; script nodes of a graph outside the pinned checkouts need the owner's allow_scripts. Follow jobs with jobs(action="status").

- `action` (Literal['status', 'tools', 'check', 'validate', 'generate', 'run'], required): Action to perform.
- `sim` (str | None, default `None`): run (required): simulated SUITE/TASK, such as libero_object/0. Simulation only.
- `graph` (str | None, default `None`): validate/run (required): workflow directory or workflow.json, in this tool's run folder or the GaP or VABAR checkout.
- `instruction` (str | None, default `None`): generate (required): the task in words, one line.
- `model` (str | None, default `None`): generate: provider model name; omit for the upstream default.
- `name` (str | None, default `None`): generate/run: run folder name under <workspace>/runs/gap; default action and time.
- `timeout_s` (float, default `3600`): generate/run: job time limit in seconds.
- `allow_concurrent_gpu` (bool, default `False`): run: knowingly start beside another GPU job or a running Isaac Sim.

<a id="eval"></a>

## `eval`: VABAR benchmark

Toolset `eval` is off until you select it with `+eval`. Reference: [PLANNING-EVAL.md](PLANNING-EVAL.md#vabar). 1 tools, listed as 1: `vabar`.

### `vabar`

VABAR benchmark from its own pinned checkout: status (pins, warmup), list (tasks), run (a task's episodes, as a job; uses the GPU), bench (a frozen cell; print_only=true returns upstream's plan, false runs it as a job), results (success table and failure reasons of a run folder). Follow jobs with jobs(action="status").

- `action` (Literal['status', 'list', 'run', 'bench', 'results'], required): Action to perform.
- `task` (str | None, default `None`): run (required): SUITE/VARIANT from list, such as tool_hanging/wrenches_level1.
- `solve` (Literal['routine', 'graph', 'idle'], default `'routine'`): run/bench: the scripted routine, a Graph-as-Policy graph, or idle.
- `graph` (str | None, default `None`): run with solve=graph: a graph label the task ships, such as gt; omit for its default.
- `episodes` (str | None, default `None`): run: '0:16', '0:100:4' or '0,4,9'; default the first episode.
- `cell` (str | None, default `None`): bench (required): benchmark cell TASK_CLASS/L<level>, such as tool_hanging/L1.
- `limit` (int | None, default `None`): bench: run only the first N instances.
- `workers` (int, default `1`): bench: worker processes, 1 to 4.
- `print_only` (bool, default `True`): bench: return upstream's resolved jobs (--print, CPU, writes nothing) without running.
- `name` (str | None, default `None`): run/bench: run folder name under <workspace>/runs/vabar; default action and time.
- `bus_timeout_s` (int | None, default `None`): run: seconds a graph's tool call may wait (--bus-timeout); default for solve=graph 180, cable suites 600, as bench does.
- `run` (str | None, default `None`): results: run folder name; omit to list the newest runs.
- `timeout_s` (float, default `21600`): run/bench: job time limit in seconds.
- `allow_concurrent_gpu` (bool, default `False`): run/bench: knowingly start beside another GPU job or a running Isaac Sim.
